prs.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
prs.author: adityuhkapoor
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json only skipped JSON pre-parsing when the field annotation was exactly `str` (`field_info.annotation is not str`). It didn't account for unions that include `str` alongside other types (e.g. `str | None`, `str | int`), so a plain string value that happens to look like JSON (a number, `null`, a bool, etc.) gets silently run through `json.loads` and corrupted into the wrong type before validation. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json only skipped JSON pre-parsing when the field annotation was exactly `str` (`field_info.annotation is not str`). It didn't account for unions that include `str` alongside other types (e.g. `str | None`, `str | int`), so a plain string value that happens to look like JSON (a number, `null`, a bool, etc.) gets silently run through `json.loads` and corrupted into the wrong type before validation. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs replace the exact same overly-narrow `annotation is not str` check in pre_parse_json with a helper that inspects union members before deciding whether to json.loads a string value. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` generalizes the skip to any union composed entirely of simple types (str, int, float, bool, NoneType), so it covers str|int and str|bool/str|float in addition to str|None. #3056's `_is_optional_str` only special-cases the str|None (Optional[str]) union, so merging it alone leaves str|int/str|bool/str|float unions still vulnerable to the same corruption bug. #2032 is the strictly broader fix for the shared root cause; #3056's one distinct contribution — unwrapping `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` union members via `_unwrap_annotated` — is worth porting into #2032 before closing it.

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 keys the dedup check on `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC int id 1 and string id "1" into the same key — that still lets a numeric id falsely collide with (or be masked by) a string id, and a string id equal to "_GET_stream" can still collide with the standalone GET stream slot. #3221 replaces this with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that keeps int/string ids distinct and is provably disjoint from `GET_STREAM_KEY`, so it covers every case #3063 covers plus these two edge cases it misses.

prs.cluster_pick_reason: Only PR that fixes the deeper correctness issue alongside the contention issue: it replaces anyio.Lock with anyio.Semaphore(1) specifically because httpx can resume/close the auth-flow generator on a different task than the one that acquired the lock, which anyio.Lock disallows (task-owned) but Semaphore does not; it also splits refresh/auth-transition serialization (flow_lock) from general token-check serialization so plain resource requests are never blocked by either. #3252 only relocates the `yield request` to after releasing the same anyio.Lock, and #2858 (per its diff) similarly narrows scope around the existing anyio.Lock - both still carry the task-affinity risk with anyio.Lock and address only the contention symptom, not the resume-on-different-task correctness gap.

UrlElicitationRequiredError) fail to unpickle because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), and self.args (set by MCPError.__init__ to (code, message, data)) doesn't match subclass constructor signatures — raising TypeError on unpickle (tracked as #2431). prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3262 fixes __reduce__ on the MCPError base class itself using __new__ + Exception.__init__ + __dict__ state restore, which bypasses every subclass constructor entirely and therefore fixes ALL MCPError subclasses generically, not just UrlElicitationRequiredError. clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs replace the exact same overly-narrow `annotation is not str` check in pre_parse_json with a helper that inspects union members before deciding whether to json.loads a string value. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` generalizes the skip to any union composed entirely of simple types (str, int, float, bool, NoneType), so it covers str|int and str|bool/str|float in addition to str|None. #3056's `_is_optional_str` only special-cases the str|None (Optional[str]) union, so merging it alone leaves str|int/str|bool/str|float unions still vulnerable to the same corruption bug. #2032 is the strictly broader fix for the shared root cause; #3056's one distinct contribution — unwrapping `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` union members via `_unwrap_annotated` — is worth porting into #2032 before closing it.

clusters.pick_reason: #3262 fixes __reduce__ on the MCPError base class itself using __new__ + Exception.__init__ + __dict__ state restore, which bypasses every subclass constructor entirely and therefore fixes ALL MCPError subclasses generically, not just UrlElicitationRequiredError. Its test suite also imports and exercises NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError, demonstrating the fix generalizes. #2555 only adds a bespoke __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so any other MCPError subclass with a non-matching constructor signature would still hit the same TypeError on unpickle. #2478 also patches the base class but via a _restore_mcp_error dispatcher that special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError (calling .from_error) vs. everything else (.from_error_data) — this requires updating the dispatcher every time a new subclass needs custom reconstruction, whereas #3262's __dict__-restore approach needs no per-subclass logic at all.

clusters.pick_reason: Only PR that fixes the deeper correctness issue alongside the contention issue: it replaces anyio.Lock with anyio.Semaphore(1) specifically because httpx can resume/close the auth-flow generator on a different task than the one that acquired the lock, which anyio.Lock disallows (task-owned) but Semaphore does not; it also splits refresh/auth-transition serialization (flow_lock) from general token-check serialization so plain resource requests are never blocked by either. #3252 only relocates the `yield request` to after releasing the same anyio.Lock, and #2858 (per its diff) similarly narrows scope around the existing anyio.Lock - both still carry the task-affinity risk with anyio.Lock and address only the contention symptom, not the resume-on-different-task correctness gap.

members.cluster_pick_reason: Only PR that fixes the deeper correctness issue alongside the contention issue: it replaces anyio.Lock with anyio.Semaphore(1) specifically because httpx can resume/close the auth-flow generator on a different task than the one that acquired the lock, which anyio.Lock disallows (task-owned) but Semaphore does not; it also splits refresh/auth-transition serialization (flow_lock) from general token-check serialization so plain resource requests are never blocked by either. #3252 only relocates the `yield request` to after releasing the same anyio.Lock, and #2858 (per its diff) similarly narrows scope around the existing anyio.Lock - both still carry the task-affinity risk with anyio.Lock and address only the contention symptom, not the resume-on-different-task correctness gap.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys the dedup check on `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC int id 1 and string id "1" into the same key — that still lets a numeric id falsely collide with (or be masked by) a string id, and a string id equal to "_GET_stream" can still collide with the standalone GET stream slot. #3221 replaces this with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that keeps int/string ids distinct and is provably disjoint from `GET_STREAM_KEY`, so it covers every case #3063 covers plus these two edge cases it misses.
